hardware_revision: v1 (the only revision of the Entropy32 Recorder design in this repo's KiCad/)
physical_source_type: background radiation + 2% thoriated tungsten welding electrodes, cut into pieces
source_geometry: electrode pieces loose in a glass jar
source_distance: jar placed beside the detector; distance not measured
shielding_or_enclosure: source contained in a glass jar; no detector shielding recorded
recorder_hardware: Entropy32 Recorder (ATmega328P, Arduino Nano form factor)
timestamp_resolution: 4 us (Arduino AVR micros(): Timer0, prescaler 64, 16 MHz); all 2,000,000 raw_timer_ticks values are multiples of 4
overflow_extension_method: host-side unwrap (tools/edge_timing.py): accumulate (raw[i]-raw[i-1]) mod 2**32 between consecutive edges
other_environment_notes: Recorder D2 input fed from the GMC-320S 3.5 mm audio jack. GMC-320S ran on its own internal battery, topped up periodically over USB from a portable charger during the capture. Recorder connected over USB serial to a laptop running tools/capture_serial_to_csv.py. Detector dead time estimated at ~750 us on an oscilloscope; shortest observed interval 724 us.
